newsitem.title: USA: Seagull may raise C$350 mln plus from sale.
newsitem.headline: Seagull may raise C$350 mln plus from sale.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp could raise more than C$350 million (US$250 million) from the sale of its Canadian assets, analysts say.

"All kind of people are looking at properties from royalty trusts to aggressive buyers such as Canadian 88 Energy Corp, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Talisman Energy Inc and Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd," said Scott Inglis, analyst at FirstEnergy Capital Corp in Calgary. Seagull's reserves are 42.7 million barrels oil equivalent on 375,000 acres and 400,000 undeveloped acres.
The reserves are 85 percent natural gas and located mostly in Alberta, the company said.

Seagull said that it would take advantage of the high prices being paid by energy companies for North American assets and the deal, which is expected to close in the fall, would free up money for investment overseas, primarily Egypt.
"The fact that prices for North American reserves have pushed up is a factor, but the primary reason is that we see better opportunities overseas," said Seagull spokesman Alan Payne.
The Seagull move comes hard on the heels of an announcement by Amoco Corp that it would sell 15 percent of its U.S. reserves and invest the money internationally.
Analysts expect more property sales as companies continue restructuring in an attempt to cut costs and realize higher impact exploration and production possibilities.
"You are always seeing companies position themselves and the pace of activity is going to pick up," said Ron Barone, analyst at PaineWebber in New York.

Unlike the Amoco sale, where exploiting the reserves is of a much higher cost than the company's average, the production costs at Seagull's Canadian assets of $3.04 per barrel of oil equivalent are roughly in line with production costs of $3.30 per BOE elsewhere in the company.
Seagull said that the proceeds for the sale would in part be used to reduce the company's debt to capital ratio, currently 48 percent. Payne said the long-term target was a ratio of 40 percent.

Earlier Wednesday, Seagull said it had retained an investment banking firm to explore strategic options for its Canadian unit, Seagull Energy Canada Ltd, and hoped to reach a decision on the unit by early autumn.

Seagull on Tuesday announced that it had succesfully completed a well on its 100 percent owned South Hurghada concession in Egypt and expects to start trucking oil from the oilfield at the rate of 800 barrels per day by the third quarter of this year, rising to 4,000 BPD by year end.
The company is also producing from its Qarun field in Egypt at the rate of 40,000 barrels per day.

Although Seagull may quit Canadian exploration and production, it will still drill 27 exploration wells in the U.S. this year and expects to replace more U.S. reserves in 1997 than it did last year. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
